# aeneid-002 — review (I.102–197)

Adversarial review in two passes. Pass 1: every unit, field by field (`n` labels, Latin → `l`, `l` ↔ `i`,
remembered English in `i`/`l`, speech marks, factual claims), plus a hand scansion of all 96 lines set
against the scanner's output. Pass 2: re-read of the edited file, three more changes. All edits made by
script. `t`, `p`, `ln`, `v` are unchanged (checked against HEAD); 15 `l`, 27 `i`, 12 `n` and `about` changed.

**Counts:** Major 3 · Medium 19 · Low 28 · scan fixes added 9 · refused/verified-and-kept 22.

Remembered English: the version the draft kept echoing is Fairclough's Loeb prose (1916). It is public domain,
but the rule is the same for every known version: distinctive overlaps were rephrased. The check was made
from memory, so treat it as a careful check, not a word-for-word collation.

## Major (false label or broken `l`)

1. **#11 (I.116–117) `l`** — "and the racing swallows her in the sea whirlpool" was garbled. Now "and the racing whirlpool swallows her in the sea."
2. **#25 (I.138–139) `n`** — "'datum (est)' agrees with the nearer noun" is false: the nearer noun is `tridentem` (masc.). Now: neuter, agreeing with `imperium`, the first and weightier noun, or with the pair taken as one.
3. **#44 (I.174) `n`** — `excudit` was labelled a narrative present. The metre needs a long u (ex-cū-dit, 5th foot `cū dĭt Ă`), so it is the perfect, like `succepit`, `dedit`, `rapuit`. Note rewritten.

## Medium

4. **#7 `l`** — "rocks which the Italians, out in mid-waves, call the Altars" put the Italians out at sea. Now "rocks out in mid-waves which the Italians call the Altars".
5. **#43 `l`** — "disembarking, the longed-for the Trojans take possession of, the sand" was garbled, and `egressi` is perfect. Now "having landed, of the longed-for sand the Trojans take possession".
6. **#21 `n`** — `quos` called "a connecting relative of a kind". It is an ordinary relative whose antecedent is the `vos` of 132. Fixed.
7. **#11 `n`** — "vortex… the older vowel, like 'volgus' and 'divom'". vortex/vertex is o for e, while volgus and divom are o for u. Now: from `vorto`, the old spelling of `verto`.
8. **#42 `n`** — "thirteen are missing; they will come back". One of the thirteen, Orontes' ship, sank (I.584 *unus abest… submersum*). Corrected. (Line 381 *Bis denis… navibus*, twenty ships, checked in the source: true.)
9. **about** — "one goes down with all hands" overclaims. Now "one goes down before Aeneas's eyes".
10. **#36 `n`** — Servius on the harbour (flagged as unverified). It cannot be checked from the repo. I kept it, reworded to what I am confident Servius says (that the place is the poet's invention, his *topothesia* note on 159): "the ancient commentator Servius already took the place as the poet's own invention." If the owner wants only repo-verifiable claims, delete this sentence.
11. **#7 `n`** — "which reefs exactly was already disputed in antiquity" was unverified, so I deleted it. The note now says only that the reefs lie between Sicily and Africa.
12. **#16 `n`** — "Readers have argued over the pairing since antiquity" was unverified, so I deleted it.
13–22. **Strong echoes of a known version, rephrased:** #0 `l`+`i` ("shrieking from the North", "strikes full"); #6 `i` ("seethes with sand"); #13 `l`+`i` (the `l` was nearly verbatim: "Now the stout ship of Ilioneus, now that of brave Achates…"); #20 `l`+`i` ("divine assent", "Do you now dare, you winds"); #36 `i` ("deep within a long inlet"); #37 `l`+`i` ("barrier of its sides, on which every wave", "an island forms a harbour"); #43 `i` ("stretch their brine-soaked… on the"); #44 `i` ("strikes a spark from flint, catches the fire in leaves"); #46 `i` ("Antheus, storm-tossed… the arms of Caicus on a high stern"); #50 `i` ("carrying their heads high with branching antlers").

## Low

23–40. **Lighter echoes, rephrased:** #2 `l`+`i` (prow swings round), #3 `l`+`i` (in a heap a sheer mountain of water), #4 `i` (hang on the crest), #7 `i` (seizes and flings on hidden rocks — the Italians call them the Altars), #8 `i`, #12 `i` ("Here and there swimmers…"), #15 `i`, #16 `i` (gazing out over the deep), #17 `i` (escape her brother), #19 `l` (confidence in your birth), #25 `i` (the dread trident), #28 `i`, #32 `l` (the base rabble), #38 `i`, #47 `i`, #48 `i`, #49 `l`+`i`, #51 `i` (stretched… on the ground).
41. **#32 `i`, house rendering I.150** — "frenzy finds its own weapons" was too close to familiar versions ("fury finding weapons"). Now "their frenzy arms them with whatever lies to hand", which matches the note. `new-renderings.md` updated.
42. **#8 `l`** — "and with a rampart encircles of sand" reworded to "and encircles them with a rampart of sand" (coherence wins the tie).
43. **#22 `l`** — "but better it is the stirred-up to settle waves" reworded to "but it is better the stirred-up waves to settle."
44. **#42 `l`** — "Here" for `huc` (motion) changed to "To this place".
45. **#7 `n`** — "'Eurus', in the next line": Eurus is in line 110, two lines on. Fixed.
46. **#32 `n` + about** — "first simile" changed to "first full-scale simile" (I.82 already has *velut agmine facto*).
47. **#32 `n`** — `volgus` was compared with `vortex`, which has a different vowel change. Now compared with `volnus`/`vulnus`.
48. **#33 `n`** — dropped "readers have tried to name him" (unverified).
49. **#21 `n`** — dropped "Homer's angry gods threaten in full" (an unsupported generalisation).
50. **#49 `n`** — "armour-bearer" (a title) softened to what the line says: he carries the weapons.
51. **#37 `n`** — `quibus` gloss aligned with the revised `l` ("on (against) which").

## Refused / checked and kept (22)

- **1.129** (packet flag, COSTLY 2.0): scanner correct (Trō-ăs, -as long by position before c). No fix.
- **1.120** Ilionei synizesis, **1.131** dehinc monosyllable and Eu-, **1.141** Aeolus, **1.157** Defessi Aeneadae (Aenĕădae, -i elided), **1.160** obiectu (consonantal i), **1.195** deinde (2 syllables), **1.111** urguet: hand-scanned, scanner correct. The notes' synizesis claims for Ilionei and dehinc are therefore true.
- Every other line read against the scanner: no further error found.
- Cross-references checked against `source/aeneid-greenough.json`: 10 (pietate), 11 (irae), 52–54 (cave-prison), 57 (temperat), 58–59 (maria ac terras caelumque… ferant: kept, "exactly" is fair), 81–83 (winds released), 94–101 (talia), 149, 152, 153, 197, 381 (twenty ships). All correct.
- Homeric/Hesiodic parallels kept as correct: Od. 5 (wave after the wish to have died at Troy), Od. 12 (helmsman struck), Il. 15 (lots of the three brothers), Il. 13 (Poseidon's chariot, sea-beasts greet him), Il. 2 (assembly like waves), Od. 9 (harbour needing no cables or anchor-stones), Od. 13 (Phorcys, cave of the nymphs), Od. 10 (look-out, then one great stag), Od. 5 end (ember simile, offered only as "compare"), Od. 3 (waves like mountains, so "aquae mons… a picture from the Odyssey's storms" stands), Hesiod Th. (winds sons of Astraeus and Eos).
- `silici` as a dative of separation (#44): kept, a standard parse with a compound of ex-.
- "Quos ego" `l` "Whom I —" / `i` "You whom I —": literal and unavoidable, not a distinctive echo. House rendering kept.
- `Troas` "with short -as" (#17): true of the vowel; it is long only by position in 129. Kept.
- Shields on the sterns marking captains' ships (#46) and the late-Republican riots (#32): traditional and interpretive, kept.
- Speech marks: Neptune's speech opens with “ on unit #19 (132) and closes with ” on #27 (141); Aeneas's speech opens in the next part (198). Correct; `t` untouched.
